cards.explanation: The answer is "Follow Me." Jesus saw Levi, a tax collector, sitting at the tax booth, and He told him, "Follow Me." Just two words, friends. Short enough to fit on a sticky note.

The answer is that Levi gets up and leaves everything. Luke says Levi "…got up, left everything, and followed Him." Jesus told him to follow, and Levi got up. The text says he left everything, friends, and I'd have a hard time leaving a counter full of warm dough.

The answer is tax collectors. Luke says "A large crowd of tax collectors was there…" Levi himself was a tax collector. So this was a banquet at a tax collector's house with a large crowd of tax collectors, friends. Bring your own coworkers to the party and you get the same crowd.

The answer is False. The text says a large crowd of tax collectors was there, "…along with others who were eating with them." So there were people at that table who weren't tax collectors. It was a full house, friends, and I love a full house.

The answer is eating with tax collectors and sinners. The Pharisees and their scribes ask, "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?" They bring the complaint to the disciples, not straight to Jesus. It's the kind of question you ask while looking at the guest list, friends.
The answer is False. Jesus says, "It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but the sick." It's the sick who need a doctor, friends. And He's answering the complaint about who He's eating with.

The answer is repentance. Jesus says, "I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners, to repentance." He's still answering the complaint about His dinner guests, friends. The call goes to the very folks the Pharisees were pointing at.

The answer is eating and drinking. The Pharisees and scribes say, "John’s disciples and those of the Pharisees frequently fast and pray, but Yours keep on eating and drinking." They're comparing the groups side by side, like a stats chart in the break room. Fasting and praying on one side, eating and drinking on the other, friends.

The answer is fast. Jesus asks, "Can you make the guests of the bridegroom fast while He is with them?" The picture is a wedding, friends, and the bridegroom is right there with His guests. Nobody hands out a diet plan at that party.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "…the time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from them; then they will fast." The words are plain, friends, and I think they're a heavy thing to hear. He says it right in the middle of an answer about a wedding.

The answer is False. Jesus says the new garment gets torn, and "…the patch from the new will not match the old." So you ruin the new one and the old one still looks off, friends. I've had cookie days like that.

The answer is that the skins burst and the wine spills. Jesus says, "…the new wine will burst the skins, the wine will spill, and the wineskins will be ruined." Wineskins were containers for wine, friends. Old skins and new wine don't mix, and Jesus says the skins are ruined and the wine spills.

The answer is new. Jesus says, "…new wine is poured into new wineskins." New goes with new, friends. That's the way around the problem He just described. Even I'd rather put fresh dough in a fresh bowl.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "…no one after drinking old wine wants new, for he says, ‘The old is better.’…" It's a simple picture of how comfortable the old can feel, friends. A favorite recipe does that to me.
